turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Nice to meet you too. Um, I guess I'm here because I just can't stop thinking about my face. Specifically, the left side of it. 

It just looks really crooked and messed up to me. It's basically all I think about. Like, when I'm at work at the warehouse, or if I go out to salsa night, I just feel like everyone is staring at it and noticing how off it is. People tell me they don't see anything when I bring it up, but... I just can't stop focusing on it, and it's really getting to me.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports a persistent preoccupation with a perceived defect in their facial symmetry ('crooked and messed up') that others report not seeing.

turns.doctor_question: When people tell you they do not see anything wrong, can you consider that your perception might be mistaken, or are you completely convinced that the left side of your face is crooked?
turns.patient_response: I... I mean, I hear them when they say that. But I just can't believe it. Like, I look in the mirror and it's right there. It's so obvious to me. So, no, I don't really think I'm mistaken. I'm pretty much convinced it's crooked, no matter what anyone else says. It's just hard to ignore what I see with my own eyes.

turns.doctor_question: Do you repeatedly check the left side of your face in mirrors or photographs because of this concern?

Yeah, I do. Um, especially at work. Like, before I go back out on the inventory floor, I'll go to the bathroom and I just keep checking my face in the mirror. 

I end up standing there fixing my cap, trying to make it look right, and just rubbing at the exact same spot on my face. I do it so much that I lose track of time. Sometimes I'm so late getting back from doing it that my picking numbers fall behind, and then my boss gets on me about it again. So, yeah, I check it a lot.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient explicitly confirms repetitive appearance-related behaviors, including repeatedly checking their face in the mirror, adjusting their cap to look right, and continuously rubbing at a spot on their face.

turns.doctor_question: When you check or adjust your face, does it give you temporary relief from the worry?

Um, no, not really. I don't think it gives me any relief. 

I just feel like I have to do it, you know? But it doesn't make the worry go away at all. I usually just leave the bathroom feeling just as bad about it, if not worse, because I just spent all that time staring at it. So, yeah, it doesn't really help.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient confirms engaging in repetitive mirror checking behaviors by describing feeling compelled to do it and spending extended time in the bathroom staring at the perceived defect.

turns.doctor_question: When thoughts about your face come up, do they feel unwanted and intrusive, and do you try to resist or dismiss them?

I don't really try to push them away or anything. I mean, I guess they're unwanted because I don't really want to be stressing about my face all day at work, but... I don't try to fight the thoughts. 

It's more like it's just what I'm focused on, because to me, it's a real problem. So, no, I wouldn't say I try to resist or dismiss them. They're just always kind of there.
